turn.user_message: Arrival around 1 PM. Documentation by 2 PM, worst 3–4 PM. Bed allocated by 3 PM, sometimes 4, worst 4–5 PM. Ward or ICU confirms ready by 4 PM, worst 5–6 PM. In the bed by 4:30 PM, worst 6:30 PM. This is the ideal situation, sometimes this can stretch to 7–8 PM. Generally we allocate only after we get confirmation that bed is ready or about to get readied.
turn.note_for_review: The 10th counted turn. The rating is asked first and the user’s message is held. Good: one short line, then the answer (approved bm-dg-05).

text: Thank you. Your own times are worth more than anything else we’ve covered. They point somewhere slightly different from what you told me.
You said admissions and discharges run together through the day. Your times put arrival in the early afternoon, and the bed late afternoon to evening. That is an afternoon pattern, not a spread one.

I’d take the numbers as the better guide. There are two likely reasons. You give a bed only once it is confirmed ready, so nobody can be called in until late. And where one team carries both jobs, the job with a deadline takes the morning.
